title: If You Cannot Count It
hook: The hole looks like a hole. Count it anyway.
scene: Heavy rain at night on Meeker. You need the left. A gap opens between a pickup and a dark SUV. It looks like a Ledger-shaped hole. Your foot agrees. The ride-along is still in your hands: if you cannot count it, it is not a hole. The thermos does not argue. The schedule does.
decision: A gap just opened in the left. Do you take it?

options.text: Hold until you can count a full Ledger plus a breath, then take it
options.result: You wait. The SUV closes what looked like a hole. The next gap is longer. You count it, take it, and nobody has to lift. Late on the log. Alive in the lane.

options.text: Take it now — rain makes people generous and the pickup already lifted
options.result: You put the nose in. The SUV did not lift. You make him. Horn, spray, the Ledger's shoulder in his. That was the late merge you already watched.

options.text: Nose in and force the zipper — they will make room for a bus
options.result: You write your length into a gap that was a car. He stands on it. You stand on it. Two lanes become one argument.

options.text: Match the pickup's speed in the right and wait for him to wave you in
options.result: He never waves. You sit beside him in the rain until the light. You did not count a hole. You waited for permission the arterial does not give.

debrief: Merge only into a gap you can count — your length, plus room so nobody has to swerve or stand on it. A hole you cannot count is a wish.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part one
source.teaching_target: Accept only a merge gap large enough that other drivers need not swerve, slow, or stop.
